questions.prompt: Last month's model reported RMSE 0.110; today's retrain reports 0.124. What do you need before concluding that today's model is worse?
choices: Nothing: a higher RMSE is always a worse model
The training time of both runs, to check that neither was cut short
The parameters, the code commit and the data version behind both numbers, and proof they were scored on the same validation data
A third run, so the two numbers can be averaged
questions.explanation: A metric is only comparable with another one computed on the same data by known code. Without the data version and commit, a change in RMSE can be a data change, a code change or a parameter change, and you cannot tell which.

questions.prompt: A run already logged the param lr = '0.3'. The script now calls log_param('lr', '0.5') on the same run. What does an MLflow server (and minitrack) do?
choices: Refuses it with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE: params are written once, and a run whose inputs changed later would be two runs pretending to be one
Overwrites the value, because the last write wins
Keeps both values as a history, like a metric
Stores it silently as a tag instead
questions.explanation: Params have a primary key on (run, key). Re-logging the same value is accepted so clients can retry; a different value raises 'Changing param values is not allowed'. Tags are the mutable kind of run data.

questions.prompt: A run logged rmse = 0.2 at step 3 (timestamp 100), then a slow worker logged rmse = 0.6 at step 2 (timestamp 900). Which value does the filter metrics.rmse < 0.5 compare?
choices: 0.6, because it was written last
The smallest value ever logged
The mean of all logged values
0.2, because the latest metric is the point with the highest step, then the latest timestamp
questions.explanation: MLflow keeps every point for the history and caches a latest value per key, chosen by step first and timestamp second. minitrack compares (step, timestamp, value) tuples, so a late flush of an older epoch cannot move the run's metric backwards.

questions.prompt: search_runs with the filter params.lr > '0.05' is rejected. Why?
choices: The value must be unquoted: params.lr > 0.05
Params are strings, so only =, !=, LIKE and ILIKE are allowed; ordering text such as '0.1' and '0.05' would give misleading answers
A filter needs at least two clauses joined by AND
Learning rates must be logged as tags before they can be searched
questions.explanation: The filter language is typed. Metrics are numbers and accept <, <=, >, >=; params and tags are strings and accept equality and pattern matching only. An unquoted param value is refused too. Log a value you need to range over as a metric.

questions.prompt: Serving loads models:/house-prices@champion. Version 3 was just promoted and regresses in production. What is the rollback?
choices: Download version 2's model file and register it again as version 4
Transition version 3 to the Archived stage so that Production falls back automatically
Delete version 3 so that models:/house-prices/latest returns version 2
Set the champion alias back to version 2 with one call; servers resolve the alias to version 2 on their next load
questions.explanation: An alias is a mutable pointer to one version, and versions are never rewritten. Moving the pointer is the whole rollback, and version 3 stays in the registry with its run for the post-mortem. Stages are deprecated and never fell back automatically.

questions.prompt: minitrack compare lists v2-lr-0.3 with RMSE 0.1165 and lr-0.3 with 0.1233, and warns that their data.md5 differs. What can you conclude?
choices: Nothing about the models yet: they were scored on different validation sets; evaluate both on one data version before choosing
v2-lr-0.3 is the better model, because its RMSE is lower
lr-0.3 is the better model, because it reached a similar RMSE with half the data
The warning can be ignored, because CSV exports always have different md5s
questions.explanation: A metric depends on the data it was computed on. With different data versions the difference mixes model quality with dataset difficulty. compare picks a best run per (data.md5, commit) group for exactly this reason.
